- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 3–5% in subsequent periods.
- In low sentiment (≤ 0.33) or negative sentiment (≤ -0.40), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently underreacts to sentiment shifts in early periods (e.g., 1–3 days after sentiment change); apply lagged adjustment: +0.5–1.0% for sentiment reversal days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict in high volatility periods; cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% above recent 7-day average to avoid overextension.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.33” values, model underperforms; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to compensate for low sentiment bias.
